Sean —

Thanks for the quick intro last week. We’re trying to line up a demo that includes: product (Alex/US), platform engineering (Priya/EU), and security (Mina/APAC). Our teams span PST, CET and IST timezones — we need a plan that doesn’t force anyone to stay late repeatedly.

Ideal outcome: one recurring demo cadence that rotates time windows so each region occasionally gets a daytime slot. Also we need a 20–30 minute procurement/contract sync separate from the product demo.

Can you propose preferred slots and who from your side would host each rotation? We’ll confirm attendance availability after.

Appreciate it —
Alex Romero
Head of Product
Cardinal Cloud

Alex — thanks for the context. High level proposal below; I’ll leave the deep technical walkthroughs to Mateo but I’ll own the customer relationship and the procurement touchpoint.

Proposal (Follow‑the‑Sun demo cadence):
- Week A (Americas-friendly): Tue 16:00–17:30 PDT / Wed 00:00–01:30 UTC — host: Sean (AE) — 90m product + Q&A
- Week B (EMEA-friendly): Wed 15:00–16:30 CET / Wed 14:00–15:30 UTC — host: Mateo (SE) — 90m product + infra deep-dive
- Week C (APAC-friendly): Thu 10:00–11:30 IST / Thu 05:30–07:00 UTC — host: Mateo or local APAC partner — 90m product + security slot

Rotation mechanics: rotate the three windows weekly so no region repeats an overnight slot more than once every three weeks. We’ll also keep a standing 30-minute procurement window (separate invite) — Priya, does morning CET or late US afternoon work better for you?

Next steps:
1) Confirm whether the 90m cadence and rotation frequency works for Cardinal Cloud.
2) I’ll send calendar invites (ICS) with timezone-aware times and an agenda.
3) Mateo will prepare a short security/architecture appendix for the APAC slot.

Attachments: proposed_timebands.csv (simple table of UTC/loc times)

Regards,
Sean Gallagher

Sean / Alex —

Thanks — quick tech notes from my side that will affect host assignment and agenda slices:
- Security proof points (audit logs, KMS integrations, VPC/private deployments) need a dedicated 20–30m block with the security contact on screen.
- For APAC sessions I recommend giving the SE lead 10–15m of deep-dive on latency/quantization strategy for customer-specific workloads.
- We can keep the main deck to ~40m, then breakouts: procurement (30m) and security (30m) as needed.

Host ownership suggestion: rotate hosts but have a primary SE owner (me) who will be on every meeting for continuity; rotate AE host for handoffs and executive-level questions. That reduces context switching across regions.

I built a draft agenda and an outline of the security appendix — attaching both. Also added timezone conversion notes so invites show correct local times.

-- Mateo Alvarez
